tier_reason: The README states only first-party ratios ('typically 50 times faster than SQL'; GOL build '20 times faster than an import into an SQL database'; under a tenth of SQL storage). It gives no methodology, hardware or named database. The repo's only benchmark (benchmark/benchmark_main.cpp) times GeoDesk queries alone, with no SQL baseline, so this is C at best.

corrections.caveats: First-party marketing ratios with no methodology, hardware, compiler or named baseline. 'SQL' and 'traditional SQL-based database' presumably mean PostGIS/osm2pgsql, but the README does not say so. benchmark/benchmark_main.cpp (inspected) has two Catch2 benchmarks that time only GeoDesk: 1,000 containing(Coordinate) queries on admin areas over Western Europe, and counting all buildings in the United States. They read hard-coded local Windows GOL paths (d:\geodesk\tests\*.gol) and contain no SQL comparison. The same three claims appear in the Java sibling repo clarisma/geodesk (201 stars, Apache-2.0), so the claim comes from the GeoDesk project as a whole, not from libgeodesk's C++ code specifically. geodesk.com was EGRESS_BLOCKED. Narrow OSM-only domain, and the baseline is not one of Boost.Geometry, CGAL, GEOS or R-tree, so the category fit is borderline; low confidence.

notes: README claims verified verbatim and benchmark_main.cpp read: it has no SQL baseline. Metadata matches: LGPL-3.0 (sources carry SPDX LGPL-3.0-only), 20 stars, not archived, last commit 2026-09-28. Kept at C under the 'numbers without methodology' rule, though the numbers are slogan-level.

corrections.workload: Third-party blog benchmark (rogue-modron.blogspot.com, 'Polygon Clipping: a Wrapper, a Benchmark', posted 2011-04, last updated 2013-03-04 per search snippet). Nine C/C++ polygon clipping libraries (Boost.Geometry, Boost.Polygon, Bop, CGAL, Clipper, GEOS, GPC, KBool, TerraLib) were wrapped for use from .NET and compared with SQL Server spatial types. Per snippet the versions were Clipper 5.1.2, Boost 1.53, GEOS 3.3.7 and TerraLib svn 10190. Per-test inputs are unknown.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the blog page returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, so no numbers, flags or hardware were seen, hence tier D. Per search snippets, the benchmark tested Clipper 5.1.2 (not 6.4.2) through .NET wrappers, so marshalling overhead is in every time, and the author warned it may contain errors and did not consider robustness or optimization. The same snippet says Boost.Geometry wins in a longer test and when many intersections occur, so the win is workload dependent. The SourceForge page itself has no performance claims. It marks the project obsolete and no longer maintained, superseded by Clipper2 (github.com/AngusJohnson/Clipper2, a separate rewrite). The last file release, clipper_ver6.4.2.zip, is dated 2017-02-27. A copy of the OSGeo FOSS4G geometry-libraries benchmark (svn.osgeo.org) was also EGRESS_BLOCKED.
